title: Grounding Language Models in Revealed Audience Behavior
abstract: arXiv:2611.31999v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models are increasingly used to simulate how an audience will respond to a headline or a post, and such simulators are validated against what people say. We validate them against what people do. We call a model grounded in revealed audience behavior when it is fine-tuned on records of what audiences actually clicked, liked or watched, and we ask not only whether asking a model falls short of grounding it, as prior work found, but why and where. Why: the gap is a property of the training signal, not mainly of model size or prompting. The same 8B model is right about half the time when asked which headline readers will click and 86.5% of the time when grounded in the clicks; the strongest prompting we tried only matches a text classifier; a grounded 0.6B model beats every prompted frontier model in our runs; and whether the clicks are fitted as counts or as shares makes no detectable difference in a pre-registered test. translated_title: 将语言模型锚定于受众显性行为
translated_abstract: 语言模型正越来越多地被用于模拟受众对某个标题或帖子的反应，而此类模拟器通常以人们“说”的内容作为验证基准。我们则用人们“做”的事来验证它们。当一个模型在受众实际点击、点赞或观看的记录上进行微调时，我们称其为“锚定于受众显性行为”。我们不仅追问此前研究所发现的“直接询问模型不如行为锚定”这一现象是否成立，还进一步追问差距为何存在、存在于何处。为何存在：这一差距源于训练信号本身的特性，而非主要取决于模型规模或提示方式。同一个80亿参数（8B）模型，在被直接询问读者会点击哪个标题时，正确率约为50%；而经过点击行为锚定后，正确率达到86.5%；我们尝试的最强提示方法也只能与一个文本分类器相当；在我们的实验中，一个经过行为锚定的0.6B模型击败了所有采用提示方式的前沿模型；此外，在一项预先注册的检验中，将点击数据按计数还是按份额进行拟合，未检测到任何差异。（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出将语言模型在受众真实的点击、点赞、观看记录上进行微调（即“受众显性行为锚定”），使同一个8B模型预测标题点击的准确率从约50%提升至86.5%，并证明“直接询问模型”与“行为锚定”之间的差距主要源于训练信号，而非模型规模或提示方式。
en_tdlr: Grounding language models in revealed audience behavior—fine-tuning on records of what people actually clicked, liked, or watched—raises the same 8B model's headline-click prediction accuracy from about 50% to 86.5%, showing that the gap between asking a model and grounding it stems from the training signal rather than model size or prompting.
